@@ -80,13 +80,87 @@ jobs:
             --pg-conf flix-parser.pro \
             flix/out/flix/assembly.dest/out.jar
 
+      # Compile-time counterpart to the R8 jar above. R8 removes every Scala
+      # pickle signature, so the slim runtime jar cannot be compiled against:
+      # scalac reads the Flix classes as plain Java classes and case-class
+      # companions fail to resolve. ProGuard retains the signatures under the
+      # same keep rules, so it produces the artifact consumers compile against
+      # -- 32 MB full assembly -> ~1.6 MB. See flix-parser-api.pro.
+      - name: Build compile-time API jar (ProGuard)
+        env:
+          PROGUARD_VERSION: "7.9.1"
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          curl -fsSL -o proguard.zip \
+            "https://github.com/Guardsquare/proguard/releases/download/v${PROGUARD_VERSION}/proguard-${PROGUARD_VERSION}.zip"
+          unzip -q proguard.zip
+          # The output filter keeps class files only. Any stray resource is a
+          # hazard: a root `library.properties` alone is enough to make scalac
+          # mistake this jar for the Scala library. `scala/**` is excluded so
+          # the partial copy cannot shadow the consumer's real scala-library.
+          java -Xmx4g -jar "proguard-${PROGUARD_VERSION}/lib/proguard.jar" \
+            @flix-parser-api.pro \
+            -injars flix/out/flix/assembly.dest/out.jar \
+            -outjars 'flix-parser-api.jar(ca/**.class,org/**.class)' \
+            -libraryjars "${JAVA_HOME}/jmods/java.base.jmod(!**.jar;!module-info.class)"
+
+      # Guard the three properties the API jar is useless without. Each has
+      # already been observed to fail in practice, so none is theoretical.
+      - name: Verify the API jar is compilable against
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          fail=0
+
+          # 1. Pickle signatures must survive the shrink (this is what R8 loses).
+          unzip -p flix-parser-api.jar \
+            ca/uwaterloo/flix/language/ast/SyntaxTree.class > SyntaxTree.class
+          if ! javap -v SyntaxTree.class | grep -q ScalaSignature; then
+            echo "API jar lost ScalaSignature; scalac cannot compile against it." >&2
+            fail=1
+          fi
+
+          # `unzip -Z1` lists entry names only, with no header or summary rows
+          # to parse around.
+          unzip -Z1 flix-parser-api.jar > entries.txt
+
+          # 2. No partial scala-library, which breaks scalac's symbol table.
+          if grep -qE '^scala/' entries.txt; then
+            echo "API jar bundles scala/**; it would shadow the real scala-library." >&2
+            fail=1
+          fi
+
+          # 3. Class files only -- see the library.properties hazard above.
+          if grep -vE '\.class$|/$' entries.txt | grep -q .; then
+            echo "API jar contains non-class resources:" >&2
+            grep -vE '\.class$|/$' entries.txt >&2
+            fail=1
+          fi
+
+          exit "$fail"
+
       - name: Set up Gradle
         uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
         with:
           gradle-version: "9.6.1"
 
       # Relocate Scala 2.13 into a private namespace so the parser can coexist
       # with rewrite-scala (Scala 3) on one classpath.
+      #
+      # KNOWN LIMITATION -- the shaded jar is not consumable from Scala sources.
+      # Relocating `scala` rewrites the Flix front-end's own public signatures
+      # (Lexer.run and ReadAst.Root take scala.collection.immutable.Map), so a
+      # consumer compiled against the unshaded API jar fails at runtime with
+      #   NoSuchMethodError: ca.uwaterloo.flix.language.ast.ReadAst$Root.<init>(
+      #     scala.collection.immutable.Map, ...AvailableClasses)
+      # (reproduced against this jar). It cannot be fixed by shading the
+      # consumer's compile classpath too: scalac hardwires scala.Any/scala.Predef
+      # and refuses to compile against a relocated standard library.
+      #
+      # The resolution is to make the artifact's boundary pure Java -- a small
+      # Java facade compiled INTO this jar before shading, exposing the CST with
+      # Java-typed signatures -- after which the consumer needs no Scala at all.
+      # Until then rewrite-flix consumes the UNSHADED R8 output and the shaded
+      # jar is published for evaluation only.
       - name: Shade Scala (Gradle Shadow)
         env:
           RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.validate.outputs.tag }}

           cp "tools/shade/build/libs/flix-parser-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar" "dist/flix-parser-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar"
+          # Unshaded R8 output: what rewrite-flix actually runs against today,
+          # for the reason recorded on the shade step above.
+          cp tools/shade/flix-parser-shrunk.jar "dist/flix-parser-unshaded-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar"
+          cp flix-parser-api.jar "dist/flix-parser-api-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar"

           tar -C dist -czf "dist/rewrite-m2-${RELEASE_TAG}.tar.gz" m2-repository
           rm -rf dist/m2-repository

             shasum -a 256 \
               "flix-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar" \
               "flix-parser-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar" \

           )

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+# ProGuard rules for the compile-time ("API") Flix parser artifact.
+#
+# Why this exists as a SECOND shrink, rather than reusing the R8 output:
+#
+#   R8 removes every Scala pickle signature. Scala 2.13 carries a class's type
+#   information in a `@scala.reflect.ScalaSignature` annotation, and R8 drops
+#   annotation instances whose annotation *type* was shrunk away -- and then
+#   drops them even when that type is explicitly kept and `-keepattributes *`
+#   is in force (measured: 0 of 200 sampled ca.uwaterloo.flix.language.ast
+#   classes retained ScalaSignature). Without the pickle, scalac reads the Flix
+#   classes as plain Java classes, so case-class companions fail to resolve
+#   ("Input.VirtualFile is not a value") and the consumer cannot compile.
+#
+#   ProGuard retains ScalaSignature under the same rules, so it -- not R8 --
+#   produces the compile-time artifact. R8 still produces the runtime artifact
+#   (flix-parser.pro): it is smaller, and only its bytecode has to run.
+#
+# Two further constraints, both established by experiment:
+#
+#   * The retained `scala/**` subset must be excluded. A partial scala-library
+#     on the compile classpath makes scalac fail to build its symbol table
+#     ("Missing dependency 'object scala.native'"). The consumer supplies a
+#     complete org.scala-lang:scala-library instead.
+#   * All non-class resources must be excluded. A root `library.properties`
+#     alone makes scalac misidentify this jar as the Scala library.
+#
+# `-dontoptimize` keeps the artifact a faithful ABI of the assembly; nothing
+# here is ever executed, so there is nothing to gain from optimising it.
+
+-include flix-parser.pro
+
+-dontoptimize
+
+# The pickle carriers. Keeping the annotation types is necessary (though, for
+# R8, not sufficient) for the ScalaSignature annotations to survive shrinking.
+-keep class scala.reflect.ScalaSignature { *; }
+-keep class scala.reflect.ScalaLongSignature { *; }
+
+-keepattributes RuntimeVisibleAnnotations,RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations,Signature,Scala,ScalaSig,ScalaInlineInfo
